mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes either wage inflation or policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE falls below 3.5% and continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their prior 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and price pressures, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous 12-month avg AND CPIAUCSL > previous 12-month avg
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their prior 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive monthly growth in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS and RSAFS) combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 12-month average AND UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows above its 12-month average and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a significant labor market weakening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and UNRATE rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% and continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of HOUST above its 12-month moving average.
